video_title: Perk Says Rob Pelinka Got His Job Because Of KOBE + Lakers Lack Culture

quotes.speaker: Channing Frye
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' need for a true starting rim-running center
quotes.quote: Here's what I think the Lakers need. A true starting center. A true starting rim-running center. Now, where in the hell are you going to get that from? Because those guys are valuable in the NBA.

quotes.speaker: Channing Frye
quotes.summary_phrase: Daniel Gafford as a potential Lakers center trade target

text_blocks.speaker: Channing Frye
text_blocks.text: Ooh. Is he on contract? Daniel Gafford is a crazy name. That would change a lot, especially if you want to say, 'Hey, Luka, we're going all in with you, we'll go get Daniel Gafford.'

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Rob Pelinka's accountability and job origin with the Lakers

text_blocks.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
text_blocks.text: They are hired other people alongside Rob Pelinka, right? Like there's other people that have been GMs.

text_blocks.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
text_blocks.text: It's time for Rob Pelinka, it's time for Rob Pelinka, you know, have a level of accountability and it's better to have three sets of eyes than one set of eye. For too long Rob Pelinka has had to answer to no one. And I love Rob Pelinka, but let's just keep it a buck, okay? Rob Pelinka got the job when he first got it because of Kobe. Let's just, we're just here, let's just be real. And since then, yes, one NBA championship, but Rob Pelinka has not been too powerful over the last three, four years.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' expectation of winning championships every season
quotes.quote: You know the energy, it's the same in Boston. It's championships or bust. It's not about putting butts in the seats, it's not about selling jerseys, it's not about selling tickets. It's championships or bust. Every season, the fans come in with the expectation of winning a championship. That's what they need to get back to. Kobe Bryant, God rest his soul, was here, his expectations for the Lakers will still be win championships.

quotes.speaker: Channing Frye
quotes.summary_phrase: Debate on Lakers' culture building versus winning championships

text_blocks.speaker: Channing Frye
text_blocks.text: I think Rob needs somebody who can go get like more things like get you another Luke Kennard. I think the Rui's development has been amazing. Hiring JJ is a great thing. So, as much as Rob has, you know, been bad, Rob also is doing things now that are putting the Lakers in a position to be to have a sense of culture. What is a Lakers guy now? What is a Lakers guy?

text_blocks.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
text_blocks.text: Culture? Ain't no, the only thing, the only thing cultural is fucking championships. Don't come talk about building no fucking culture. They want to win. They have to build a culture to win. No, you got to get the personnel in there to win. Wembanyama, OKC, Minnesota, none of them fuckers are going anywhere. You have to match personnel.

text_blocks.speaker: Channing Frye
text_blocks.text: You just named the three best cultures in the NBA. What are you talking about? Dude, the San Antonio culture for the last 30 years has been the best. OKC's culture has been the best since Sam Presti got there. And Minnesota, you look at their culture, they're bringing guys off the bench. We got to look at our piece of paper, who the hell's this? Coming in being dogs. Coming in, whatever Connelly, there we go, there we go. He came in there and said, 'Yo, we're going to play this way.' And look at the success that they've had when they went, everyone didn't believe in the two big lineup. Western Conference Finals, Western Conference Finals, second round, competing. So, the Lakers need to start building their culture so that they can add great players to that culture to win chips. That's all I'm saying.

text_blocks.speaker: Allie Clifton
text_blocks.text: Low key, that was actually really funny how she was making that point and then he did, he named the best three cultures in the NBA. I love you, Perk.
